**Verdict: FAIL** on DG0 round 13. The candidate is `sha256:c3364ac2…fb79` at commit `6c61f2e`. HEAD is `a733aaf`, which only adds delivery metadata after the freeze, and the recomputed candidate ID matches.

My earlier finding F-DG0-140 is fixed. The new sandbox wrapper added to fix it, `tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh`, can itself be escaped by an agent running at the same time, so I'm raising a new High finding.

**Earlier finding re-verified**
- **F-DG0-140 (Critical): fixed, CLOSED_VERIFIED.**
  - On the round-12 commit `7f09967`, my script shows the runner's unsandboxed Python helpers loading fake `json`, `hashlib`, `subprocess` and `uuid` modules planted by an agent.
  - On the candidate they load none, whether the agent's working directory is the repo root or a subdirectory.
  - The runner now switches to `/` before starting its helpers and runs every one with `python3 -I -B`, and its regression test passes.

**New findings**
- **F-DG0-141 (High, mandatory violation)**, in `tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh:19-22`.
  - **Cause:** the script puts its fresh clone under `/tmp/claude-0`, a temp folder every sandboxed agent can write to. It then runs `git checkout` there outside bubblewrap, before the sandboxed step starts.
  - **Attack:** an agent running at the same time as the orchestrator (a background shell loop is enough) adds a git "smudge" filter to the clone's config. The orchestrator's checkout then runs that filter with the orchestrator's own privileges.
  - **Reproduced 3 of 3 times:** the filter ran 1154 times and wrote into the stand-in repository's `tools/gates/`, which is read-only inside the sandbox.
  - **Second effect:** the clone stays writable from outside during the sandboxed run (about 20 s), so a concurrent agent can also swap files and make the pre-freeze checks pass on code that isn't the committed revision.
  - **Why it matters:** the threat model says this is *mechanically prevented* (D-026).
  - **Suggested fix:** put the work directory where no agent can write, and do the clone and checkout inside the sandbox too.
- **F-DG0-142 (Low, not mandatory)**, a documentation contradiction that doesn't bite until P1.
  - D-026 says the orchestrator never runs agent-writable code outside a sandbox.
  - Residual #3 in the threat model makes dependency installation an unsandboxed orchestrator step, so install scripts in an agent-written `package.json` would run outside the sandbox.
  - I'd accept this as an observation at DG0 if it's resolved before the first P1 dependency install.

**Checks run**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Candidate ID recomputed, post-freeze commits metadata-only | PASS |
| Node tests (69/69) and Python tests (14) | PASS |
| `prefreeze.sh DG0` in a fresh clone (all 10 checks) | PASS |
| F-DG0-140 old-versus-new reproduction | PASS |
| Review of every change since round 12 | FAIL (F-DG0-141, F-DG0-142) |
| `sandbox-run.sh` escape attempt | FAIL (reproduced 3/3) |
| Secrets scan of text files and new run transcripts | PASS (no credential values) |

The rest of the scope, including the write guard, scopes, schemas, candidate hashing, CSV and schema parsing, and the source scripts, is unchanged since round 12, so my earlier closures there still hold. I judge the runner's new rule for ignoring empty sandbox stub files acceptable: it can't hide a file with content, a symlink, or a change to a tracked file.

Requirements checked: REQ-DLV-006, 007, 013, 022, 023, 026.

**Files written:** my review record and both side files validate against their schemas, and all 33 evidence paths exist. I modified no implementation source and deleted my temporary clones. Everything is in `docs/delivery/`:
